stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Fig trees and the tiny wasps that pollinate them are often described as perfectly paired: one wasp species to one fig species. Ecologists expected this pairing to loosen wherever two fig species bloom side by side, but surveys of 40 such sites found nearly every wasp carrying pollen from just one host. At a forty-first site in Borneo, ______ wasps of a single species were routinely found dusted with pollen from both flowering figs.
explanation: Before you look at the choices, name the two things being compared and what each one shows. The 40 surveyed sites are one case: there, wasps stayed loyal to a single host. The Bornean site is a parallel case described in the same terms (two figs blooming side by side), but there the result flips, because the wasps carried pollen from both figs. Two parallel cases with opposite results call for a comparison-contrast word, so 'by contrast' is the logical transition.

A.why: You saw one specific site come after a general finding about many sites and reached for an example word. An example has to agree with the claim it illustrates. The Bornean wasps break the one-host pattern found at the 40 sites, so they can't illustrate it. The site is also a forty-first site, not one of the 40, so it isn't a sample drawn from that group.

C.why: You noticed that the Bornean wasps did what ecologists had expected, so you treated the sentence as a confirmation. A transition links the blank sentence to the sentence just before it, though, and that sentence reports what the surveys actually found: loyalty to one host. 'Indeed' would mean the Bornean site strengthens that finding, when in fact it goes against it.

D.why: You assumed that two figs blooming together caused the wasps to stray. The previous sentence says the opposite: at 40 sites with exactly that setup, the wasps did not stray. Nothing in the passage presents the Bornean result as following from what came before. It is a different outcome under the same conditions, not a consequence.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Living trees in warm, wet forests tend to have smooth-edged leaves, while trees in cooler forests more often have toothed edges. For that reason, paleobotanists use the share of toothed fossil leaf types to estimate ancient temperatures. In the lower beds of one Wyoming quarry, fewer than one leaf type in five is toothed, which points to a near-tropical climate. Leaves from the quarry's upper beds, ______ are toothed in more than half of their types, a sign that the region later cooled.
explanation: The blank sentence has to connect to the sentence just before it. Name each subject and its attribute. The lower beds have few toothed leaf types, which means warm conditions. The upper beds have mostly toothed leaf types, which means cool conditions. Both sentences use the same frame (which beds, what share of leaf types is toothed, what climate that implies), and the attribute flips. Two parallel cases with opposite attributes call for 'by contrast.'

A.why: This is the trap that survives the first insight. You noticed that the upper beds fit the general rule in the first sentence (toothed leaves go with cool climates), so they looked like an example of it. But the blank links the upper beds to the sentence right before it, about the lower beds, and the upper beds aren't an example of the lower beds. They are the opposite case. The lower beds were already the passage's illustration of the method, and the upper beds are set against them.

B.why: You read the passage as a mechanism followed by an outcome and took 'the region later cooled' as a result. But the toothed upper-bed leaves don't follow from the smooth lower-bed leaves described in the previous sentence. They are evidence of cooling, not a consequence of anything in that sentence.

D.why: You noticed that both sentences describe quarry beds and use the same method, and you took that as similarity. 'Similarly' requires the same attribute, though. The lower beds are mostly smooth-edged and warm, while the upper beds are mostly toothed and cool, so the attribute is reversed.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Long-span bridges in regions with harsh winters are typically built with many expansion joints: gaps in the deck, spanned by interlocking steel plates, that open as the structure contracts in the cold and close as it swells in the heat. Engineers count on these joints to keep the deck from cracking, and some northern spans carry more than a dozen. The Halvard Viaduct in Arctic Norway, ______, was cast as a single unbroken deck, its seasonal movement absorbed entirely by slender piers designed to bend.
explanation: Line up the two subjects and what each one does. Typical harsh-winter bridges rely on many expansion joints. The Halvard Viaduct, also in a harsh-winter region, has no joints at all and is a single unbroken deck. The setting matches but the design is the opposite, so you need a contrast word: 'by contrast.'

A.why: You saw one specific Arctic bridge after a claim about harsh-winter bridges and treated it as a sample. But an example has to agree with the general claim, and this bridge has no joints. It goes against the tendency, so it can't illustrate it.

C.why: You read the piers as the result of something in the sentence before. Nothing earlier causes the Viaduct to skip joints. The earlier sentences describe a different design, not a reason for this one.

D.why: 'Likewise' needs the second case to share the attribute. You may have matched on the shared setting (harsh winters), but the attribute that matters, how the deck handles movement, is reversed.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Eighteenth-century European dye works drew on two main sources of red: madder root, cheap and widely grown, and cochineal, an insect dye imported from the Americas at great cost. Most workshops kept cochineal for luxury silks and used madder for everything else. One Lyon dyer whose ledgers survive, ______, bought cochineal by the barrel and used it even on the coarse wool sold for soldiers' coats.
explanation: The general practice was cochineal for silk only and madder for everything else. The Lyon dyer used cochineal on cheap wool too. That is one workshop set against most workshops, with the practice flipped, so 'in contrast' is right.

A.why: 'One Lyon dyer' after 'most workshops' looks like a sample from the group. Check whether the case agrees with the claim first. This dyer broke the rule, so it isn't an example of it.

B.why: 'Moreover' adds another point in the same direction. The dyer's habit doesn't add to the description of normal practice. It goes against it.

D.why: Nothing in the earlier sentences explains why this dyer spent lavishly. If anything, cochineal's high cost would predict the opposite, so a conclusion word reverses the logic.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Most reef fish that change sex do so only once and in one direction: they begin life as females, and if the dominant male of their group disappears, the largest female becomes male. Biologists studying the coral goby, ______, have found individuals that switch from male to female and then, when the makeup of their group shifts again, back.
explanation: Most reef fish change once, female to male. Coral gobies change in either direction and more than once. Two cases are set side by side and the attribute flips, so a contrast word fits: 'however.'

B.why: You took the goby as a closer look at the same pattern. 'Specifically' restates the earlier claim more precisely, but the goby breaks both parts of that claim ('only once' and 'in one direction') instead of sharpening it.

C.why: The loss of a dominant male causes a change in typical reef fish. It doesn't cause gobies to switch both ways. You linked a mechanism from one group to an outcome in another.

D.why: Both sentences are about sex change, so they look alike, but 'similarly' requires the same pattern. The goby's pattern is the reverse of the rule and also repeats.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Among songbirds, singing has traditionally been described as a male activity: in most temperate species, females are silent or limit themselves to short contact calls, and field guides long treated elaborate song as a reliable sign that a bird was male. The female plain-tailed wren of the Andes, ______, performs a rapid duet with her mate, the two birds alternating syllables so precisely that listeners hear a single voice.
explanation: The subjects are females of most temperate species and the female plain-tailed wren. The first group is mostly silent, and the wren sings elaborately. Same frame, opposite attribute, so 'by contrast' fits.

A.why: A single named species after a general statement about songbirds looks like an illustration. But this female sings, which goes against the general claim, so it can't be an example of it.

B.why: Nothing about the field guides' view causes the wren to sing. 'Therefore' would make the wren's song follow from a claim it actually overturns.

D.why: 'Indeed' strengthens the earlier claim. The wren's duet undercuts the idea that song marks a male, so this transition points the wrong way.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: In most intaglio printmaking, the artist makes a line by taking metal away: an engraver cuts grooves into a copper plate with a burin, and an etcher lets acid eat them out. Ink is wiped into these recesses and pressed onto damp paper. Collagraphy, ______, builds the printing surface up rather than cutting it down: the artist glues sand, string, or fabric onto a board, and ink collects in the textures added to it.
explanation: Engraving and etching make the image by removing material. Collagraphy makes it by adding material. Two methods are set side by side and one attribute (subtracting vs. adding) is reversed, which calls for 'conversely.'

A.why: Collagraphy is one printmaking technique named after a general description of printmaking, so it feels like a sample. But it does the opposite of 'taking metal away,' so it can't illustrate that claim.

B.why: The step words in the passage ('wiped,' 'pressed') may have made you read this as the next stage of a process. Collagraphy is a separate technique, not a step that follows printing.

C.why: 'Accordingly' says collagraphy follows from how engraving and etching work. It doesn't. It is a different approach, not a consequence.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Over most of the globe, air grows colder with altitude, losing roughly 6.5°C for every kilometer it rises; this steady cooling is why summits hold snow in midsummer while the valleys below swelter. In a temperature inversion, ______, a layer of warm air settles above cooler air near the ground, trapping smoke and haze beneath it until sunlight or wind breaks the layer apart.
explanation: Normal air gets colder as you go higher. In an inversion, warm air sits above cool air, so temperature rises with height. The two conditions are described with the same frame and the attribute flips, so 'by contrast' is correct.

A.why: An inversion is a specific atmospheric condition, so it seems like a sample of how air behaves. But it reverses the normal pattern instead of showing it.

C.why: The trapped smoke looks like an outcome, but it results from the inversion itself, not from the normal cooling described earlier. Normal cooling doesn't cause an inversion.

D.why: 'Additionally' just adds a further fact in the same direction. You need to see that the inversion contradicts the earlier pattern instead of adding to it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Most Carboniferous plants reproduced by spores, which require a film of water for sperm to reach the egg; that dependence kept the period's vast forests confined to swamps and floodplains. Seed ferns, ______, enclosed a fertilized embryo in a protective coat stocked with food, an arrangement that freed them to spread onto drier ground.
explanation: Most Carboniferous plants reproduced by water-dependent spores and stayed near water. Seed ferns, also Carboniferous plants, used protected seeds and moved onto dry land. One group is set beside the majority with the attribute reversed, so 'by contrast' fits.

B.why: Seed ferns belong to the Carboniferous flora the first sentence describes, so they look like a sample. But they didn't reproduce by spores and weren't confined to wet ground, so they go against the claim.

C.why: The second sentence does describe a mechanism and its effect, but that cause-and-effect sits inside the sentence. It doesn't follow from the first sentence. Spore dependence doesn't cause seed ferns to make seeds.

D.why: 'Indeed' reinforces what came before. The seed ferns' escape from the swamps undercuts the picture of forests tied to water instead of strengthening it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: In English, an adjective almost always comes before the noun it modifies: speakers say "red house," never "house red," and the rule holds so firmly that children rarely break it even while learning to talk. A handful of fixed phrases inherited from medieval legal French, ______, keep the adjective after the noun, as in "attorney general," "court martial," and "heir apparent."
explanation: Ordinary English puts the adjective before the noun. These legal phrases put it after. Both cases are English phrases, and word order is the attribute that flips, so you need 'by contrast.'

A.why: The legal phrases are English phrases, so they look like samples of English word order. Check the order: noun first, then adjective. They break the rule, so they can't be examples of it.

B.why: The firmness of the English rule would lead you to expect these phrases to follow it. A conclusion word gets the relationship backwards.

C.why: 'Similarly' needs the same word order in both cases. The phrases reverse it, so the two cases are opposed, not alike.
